title: Indian Diaspora Holds Bharat First Gathering in Munich Backing Democratic Mandate
excerpt: Professionals, students and families from across Germany rallied at Rindermarkt to defend India's democratic choices and counter what organisers called anti-India narratives abroad.
body:
• Members of the Indian diaspora gathered at Rindermarkt in Munich for a peaceful 'Bharat First' demonstration organised by NRIs for Bharat Rise.
  • Participants called for respect for the mandate of 1.4 billion Indians and the government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
  • Speakers singled out Germany-based online commentators, saying they do not speak for the wider Indian community in Europe.
  • For diaspora readers: the group says it will keep engaging local German audiences directly to present India's perspective in international discussions.

MUNICH — Members of the Indian diaspora in Germany gathered at Rindermarkt in central Munich for a peaceful demonstration titled 'Bharat First', organised by Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) for Bharat Rise, to express support for India's democratic mandate and counter what organisers described as anti-India narratives abroad, ANI reported.

The gathering, held on Saturday, brought together Indian professionals, students and families from across Germany. Participants called for respect for the mandate of 1.4 billion Indians and the government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, arguing that election outcomes delivered through India's democratic process should be honoured in international discussion of the country.

A Pushback Against Campaigns Abroad

According to the organisers, certain negative elements and politically motivated campaigns are attempting to weaken India's democratic image from abroad. The diaspora resolved to actively counter what it called divisive protests and to defend India's global standing through factual, patriotic narrative-building.

That framing — a contest over how India is portrayed outside its borders — was the organising theme of the event. Participants said the demonstration was intended less as a protest against any single policy than as a public assertion that India's democratic institutions and electoral verdicts deserve to be treated as legitimate by audiences in Europe and elsewhere.

Full details of the gathering were reported by ANI via Daily Prabhat.

Online Critics Singled Out

During extensive discussions at the gathering, participants directly addressed the issue of Germany-based commentators, specifically calling out YouTuber Dhruv Rathee. Diaspora leaders emphasised that self-styled online critics living in Germany do not speak for the wider Indian community across Europe, who, they said, overwhelmingly stand behind India's democratic choices, economic progress and national sovereignty.

The call-out reflects a broader friction within the diaspora over who represents Indian opinion abroad. Organisers drew a distinction between the large community of Indian professionals, students and families living and working in Germany — many of them recent migrants with close ties to India — and individual commentators whose videos and posts reach large audiences online. Their argument was that the community's own voice should carry weight alongside that online commentary.

Engaging the Local German Audience

The gathering also sought to engage with the local German community. Organisers and participants interacted with passers-by at Rindermarkt to discuss India's democratic system and development, while addressing what they described as misrepresentations of the country in international media.

Speakers emphasised that political debate was an essential part of democracy, but maintained that efforts to undermine constitutional institutions or incite hatred abroad should be opposed. That distinction — welcoming debate while rejecting what they characterised as campaigns against institutions — was repeated through the event's discussions.

The participants called for national unity, factual discourse and respect for democratic processes, reiterating their commitment to projecting India's perspective in international discussions. The Munich gathering is the latest in a series of diaspora-led public events in European cities in which Indian community groups have sought to respond directly, and in person, to criticism of India voiced overseas.
